discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators (the quantum spin Hall effect)
subfield: Condensed matter physics (topological phases of matter)
motivation: In 2005 Kane and Mele showed that time-reversal symmetry, together with spin-orbit coupling, allows a new topological class of insulators, characterised by a Z2 invariant and protected helical edge states: the quantum spin Hall effect. This changed how physicists classify matter. Band insulators, once thought trivial, were shown to carry hidden topology, and their work directly led to three-dimensional topological insulators, the periodic table of topological phases, and the search for Majorana modes. In 2007 Molenkamp and co-workers observed quantised edge conductance in HgTe quantum wells, the decisive experimental confirmation, following the Bernevig–Hughes–Zhang proposal. The 2016 prize honoured the topological concepts of Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz. The Kane–Mele–Molenkamp discovery brought topology into ordinary materials with symmetry protection. It has become a cornerstone of modern condensed matter physics, verified in many laboratories through transport and photoemission.
